title: A study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of three doses of frevecitinib in patients with severe asthma not adequately controlled with medium to high dose ICS/LABA therapy
official: A Phase 2 Randomized Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel Group Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Three Doses of Frevecitinib (KN-002) in Patients with Severe Asthma not Adequately Controlled with Medium to High Dose ICS/LABA Therapy (PANAIRAMA)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of frevecitinib
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Is capable of understanding the written informed consent, provides signed and witnessed written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures, and agrees to comply with protocol requirements.  2.	Able to understand and comply with the protocol requirements of the study, as judged by the investigator or designee.  3.	Is 18 to 75 years of age (both inclusive) at the time of signing informed consent.
2. 4.	Body mass index between [CCI] and weight [CCI] at screening.  5.	Documented physician-diagnosed asthma for at least 12 months prior to screening.  6.	Has received a physician-prescribed asthma controller regimen with medium dose or high dose ICS plus LABA, with or without additional controller medications,  for at least 6 months prior to screening and the dose of ICS and additional controller(s) must be stable for at least 4 weeks prior to screening and throughout the screening/run-in period.  •	High dose ICS equates to a total daily dose of >500 μg fluticasone propionate dry powder inhaler, or a total daily dose of >440 μg fluticasone propionate HFA or equivalent.  •	Medium dose ICS equates to a total daily dose of 250 to 500 μg fluticasone propionate dry powder inhaler or a total daily dose of 220 to 440 μg fluticasone propionate HFA or equivalent.   •	If on asthma controller medications in addition to ICS plus LABA, the dose of the other asthma controller medications (eg, leukotriene receptor inhibitors, theophylline, LAMA) must be stable for at least 4 weeks prior to the first screening visit and should remain stable throughout the treatment period.
3. 7.	Has a pre-bronchodilator FEV1 value of ≥40% and ≤80%, predicted, at screening and at Day 1.  8.	Has a post-bronchodilator reversibility of FEV1 ≥12% and ≥200 mL documented during screening (15 to 30 min after administration of 4 puffs of albuterol/salbutamol). Participants may repeat reversibility testing 1 time during screening to meet reversibility criteria if the first attempt was ≥8%.  9.	Has an ACQ-6 score of ≥1.5 during screening (ie, Visit 1 and Visit 2). 10.	[CCI]
4. 11. Has a documented history of at least 1 asthma exacerbation in the 12 months prior to the screening visit, while using medium to high dose ICS/LABA therapy (see Section 15.2 for definitions of medium to high dose ICS), requiring treatment with oral or systemic corticosteroids for at least 3 consecutive days or emergency department visit >24 hours or hospitalization, requiring systemic corticosteroids. A single depoinjectable dose or IV parenteral dose of corticosteroids will be considered equivalent to a 3-day bolus/burst of systemic corticosteroids.   12. If on allergen-specific immunotherapy, participants must be on a maintenance regimen and schedule for at least 2 months prior to screening and continue this throughout the study.  13. Has a documented chest radiograph or other imaging modality (eg, plane chest x-ray, CT, MRI) confirming no evidence of active lung disease(s) other than asthma within 3 months before the start of screening. For participants who have not had thoracic imaging within 3 months of the start of screening, a chest x-ray may be taken during the screening period, with the result available before Day 1 randomization.   14. Participants must meet all the following criteria related to asthma treatment prior to randomization:  -Acceptable inhaler, peak flow meter, and spirometry techniques during the screening/run-in period.  -Able to generate sufficient PIF (at least 60 L/min) using the [CCI] device at screening.  -≥70% compliance with expected administrations of usual asthma controller ICS/LABA during the last 14 days of the screening/run-in period.  -≥80% compliance with required use of the ePRO device within the last 14 days of the screening/run-in period. The 80% compliance is defined as completing any 11 of 14 morning ePRO entries and any 11 of 14 evening ePRO diary entries during the 14-day period before Day 1.   15. Females of childbearing potential who are sexually active with a nonsterilized male partner must use a highly effective method of contraception with low user dependence from the time informed consent is obtained in conjunction with an additional barrier method where appropriate based on the selected contraceptive method and applicable national requirements. Pregnancy risk counselling at the screening visit should be documented (n.b. hormonal contraception for female participants and female partners of male participants should be started ≥28 days prior to the treatment period). The participant must agree to continue using such precautions throughout the study and continue using such precautions for 16 weeks after the final dose of study treatment. Cessation of contraception after this point should be discussed with a responsible physician (see Section 15.1, Appendix: Contraceptive Guidance).  16. Nonsterilized males who are sexually active with a female partner of childbearing potential must use a male condom plus spermicide from Day 1 through 92 days after receipt of the final dose of study treatment and should be advised of the benefit for a partner of childbearing potential to use a highly effective method of contraception, preferably with low user dependence, as a condom may break or leak when having sexual intercourse.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Current smokers (includes tobacco or nicotine, cigarettes or e-cigarettes, vaping, or marijuana use) or participants with a smoking history of ≥10 pack years (number of pack years = number of cigarettes per day/20 × number of years smoked). Former smokers with <10 pack years must have stopped for at least 6 months prior to screening to be eligible. 2.	Previous medical history or evidence of an uncontrolled intercurrent illness that, in the opinion of the investigator and/or medical monitor, may compromise the safety of the participant in the study or interfere with evaluation of the investigational product or reduce the patient’s ability to participate in the study. Participants with a current history of angina or history of myocardial infarction, stroke, or TIAs within the past 12 months from screening are disallowed. Participants with a history of pulmonary embolic or thrombotic events, or genetic predisposition of thrombosis are disallowed. Participants with well controlled comorbid disease (eg, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, gastroesophageal reflux disease) on a stable treatment regimen for 15 days prior to screening are eligible.  3.	Any concomitant respiratory disease that, in the opinion of the investigator and/or medical monitor, will interfere with the evaluation of the investigational product or interpretation of participant safety or study results (eg, COPD, cystic fibrosis, pulmonary fibrosis, bronchiectasis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, Churg–Strauss syndrome).
2. 4.	Any clinically relevant abnormal findings in hematology, clinical chemistry, coagulation, or urinalysis (laboratory results from visit), physical examination, vital signs during the screening/run-in period which, in the opinion of the investigator, may put the participant at risk because of his/her participation in the study, or may influence the results of the study, or the participant’s ability to participate in the study.   5.	 Evidence of active liver disease including jaundice or AST, ALT, or bilirubin greater than twice the upper limit of normal. Participants with alkaline phosphatase greater than twice the upper limit of normal may be included if additional isoenzyme testing has confirmed that the elevations are not of hepatic origin. Participants with isolated bilirubin elevations may be included if they have a confirmed diagnosis of Gilbert's syndrome. 6.	History of cancer:  •	Participants who have had basal cell carcinoma or in situ carcinoma of the cervix are eligible to participate in the study provided that curative therapy was completed at least 12 months prior to screening. •	Participants who have had other malignancies are eligible provided that curative therapy was completed and have been in remission at least 5 years prior to screening.
3. 7.	Participants with an RTI that has not fully resolved by screening, or who experience an RTI during screening or at Day 1. Participants who experience an RTI during screening or at Day 1 may be rescreened once they have fully recovered.  8.	Evidence of a clinically significant infection or receiving treatment with systemic antibiotic, anti-parasitic, or antiviral medications at Day 1.  9.	Known history of active TB or a positive QFT-G test for TB during screening. Participants with a positive or indeterminate QFT-G result may be enrolled if they have ALL the following: •	No symptoms of TB: productive, prolonged cough (>3 weeks); coughing up blood; fever; night sweats, unexplained appetite loss, unintentional weight loss •	No known exposure to a case of active TB after most recent prophylaxis (prophylaxis required only if positive)  •	No evidence of active TB on chest radiograph within 3 months prior to the first dose of investigational product and have completed a course of treatment for latent TB Participants with an indeterminate QFT-G result will have repeat QFT-G testing at Week 12/EOT.   Participants with a prior history of latent TB but proved nonactive within the 3 months prior to screening and having a documented course of treatment for latent TB may be considered for enrollment. 10.	A positive hepatitis B surface antigen, or hepatitis C virus antibody serology at screening, or a positive medical history for hepatitis B or C. Participants with a history of hepatitis B vaccination without history of hepatitis B are allowed to enroll. Participants with positive hepatitis C virus serology at screening and a subsequent negative test for hepatitis C RNA may be enrolled.
4. 11. A positive human immunodeficiency virus test at screening or participant taking antiretroviral medications, as determined by medical history and/or participants verbal report.  12. History of sensitivity to any component of the investigational product formulation or a history of drug or other allergy that, in the opinion of the investigator or medical monitor contraindicates their participation.  13. Use of 5-lipoxygenase inhibitors (eg, zileuton) within 15 days prior to screening and throughout the study.  14. Use of roflumilast or azithromycin within 15 days prior to screening and throughout the study.  15. Use of oral or topical JAK inhibitors for any reason or use of immunosuppressive medication (eg, methotrexate, troleandomycin, oral gold, cyclosporine, azathioprine, intramuscular long-acting depot glucocorticoid, or any experimental anti-inflammatory therapy) within 3 months prior to screening and throughout the study.  16. Receipt of immunoglobulin or blood products within 30 days prior to screening and throughout the study.  17. Receipt of any investigational nonbiologic agent within 30 days or 5 half-lives prior to screening, whichever is longer and throughout the study.  18. Prescription of regular daily oral corticosteroids within 4 weeks prior to screening or during the screening/run-in period and throughout the study.
5. 19. Systemic glucocorticoid burst including taper within 15 days prior to screening or during the screening/run-in period and throughout the study.  20. Prescription of concomitant parenteral monoclonal antibody therapy for the management of asthma or any other condition within a specified period prior to the screening visit as below and throughout the study:  Mepolizumab: 4 months  Benralizumab: 6 months  Omalizumab: 6 months  Reslizumab: 6 months  Dupilumab: 6 months  Tezepelumab: 6 months  Others: 5 half-lives  21. Pregnant, breastfeeding, or lactating females.  22. History of chronic alcohol or drug abuse within 12 months prior to screening, as determined by the investigator.  23. Planned surgical procedures requiring general anesthesia or in-patient status for >1 day during the conduct of the study.  24. Receipt of any live or attenuated vaccines within 15 days prior to screening.  25. Participants who have undergone bronchial thermoplasty.  26. Prolonged QTcF >470 ms at screening or baseline (female) or QTcF >450 ms at screening or baseline (male).
